text:
Irene: quick signal check hitting an odd typing split between our ESM and CJS SDK builds when used in edge apps. ESM consumers infer a string overload but CJS users get `T = any` from the generic overload.

Noah: yeah that smells like moduleResolution/interop differences. can you paste the two overloads?

Irene: here, simplified:
```ts
function client<T extends object>(opts: { auth: T }): Client<T>
function client(opts: { auth: string }): Client<{ token: string }>
```
Callsite: `client({ auth: process.env.AUTH })`

In ESM + nodeNext it picks the string overload. In CommonJS/`module: "CommonJS"` tsc selects the generic and `T` becomes `any`. That leaks into downstream types and fails stricter checks on the edge runtime.

Kai: are you shipping different .d.ts shapes for .cjs vs .mjs? `export =` vs `export default` differences can change inference and overload resolution.

Irene: yes, build emits a `.cjs` wrapper and an ESM entry. Consumers using `esModuleInterop` see different symbol shapes.

Noah: pragmatic fixes: 1) reorder overloads so primitive/string overload comes first, 2) add a tiny discriminant `authKind?: 'token'` to the string overload, 3) add a narrow `auth: string | number` overload before the generic.

Kai: also document recommended tsconfig for edge consumers: `module: "ESNext"` or at least `moduleResolution: "nodeNext"`. Add a note about `skipLibCheck` hiding inference surprises.

Irene: I'll open a PR to reorder overloads and add an examples/edge-tsconfig.md with the recommended settings and a short note about `unknown` vs `any` pitfalls: prefer explicit generics if you expect structured auth objects.

devx-bot: Draft PR created: https://github.com/redwood-inference/sdk/pull/489 - includes overload reorder + examples. CI: typings-check queued. :white_check_mark:

Noah: nice. add a small failing unit-types test that asserts inferred type is Client<{ token: string }> for the env string case so we catch regressions.

Irene: will do. thanks!
